name: Yen & carry trade
summary: Yen near ¥159.1 per dollar on 20 Nov, little changed on the week; no intervention found
state: The dollar was near ¥159.1 early on 20 Nov, down 0.4% on the week and up 1.7% on the month, inside the 3% weekly and 6% monthly Watch lines (Yahoo Finance). The yen is about 2.9% stronger than its 52-week low of ¥163.9 per dollar. No Japanese currency intervention was found to 20 Nov.
for_you: The yen is weak but stable. Travellers to Japan and importers of Japanese goods face little change on the week.
rubric_hit: USD/JPY 1w move 0.61% below the 3% Watch line; USD/JPY 1m move 1.48% below the 6% Watch line
why: Cheap yen borrowing funds positions worldwide; a sharp yen rally forces those trades to unwind, as in the global sell-off of August 2024.
drivers: Bank of Japan policy, the US–Japan rate gap, JGB yields, currency intervention, risk appetite.

rubric.alert: A move of more than 5% in a week or 10% in a month, with stress spreading to other markets.
rubric.watch: A 3–5% move in a week, a 6–10% move in a month, or Japanese currency intervention.
rubric.normal: The yen moves less than 3% against the dollar in a week and less than 6% in a month.
